data.cultural_impact: The name Shivangna instills a deep connection to the rich cultural heritage of Hinduism. It is a reminder of the reverence and devotion towards Lord Shiva, one of the most essential deities in Hindu mythology. It conveys a sense of divine protection and blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shivangna holds great significance in Hindu spirituality. It symbolizes the idea of being connected to the divine and holding the qualities of Lord Shiva - endless love, detachment, tranquility, and wisdom. The name serves as a constant reminder to strive towards spiritual growth and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: The name Shivangna is a combination of Shiva and Anga. Anga was an ancient kingdom located in the eastern part of India, currently known as West Bengal and parts of Bangladesh. Shiva was a major deity worshipped in Anga during the medieval period. The name Shivangna may have originated from the reverence and devotion of the people of Anga towards Shiva.

Another historical reference suggests that Shivangna was a renowned Hindu queen of the Sena Dynasty, who ruled over the region of present-day Bengal during the late medieval period. She is believed to have been a devotee of Lord Shiva and is mentioned in various Hindu texts and folklore.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shivangna' is derived from the Hindu god Shiva and is often used in the context of goddess worship, spirituality, and yoga. On Instagram, you might find accounts dedicated to Shivangna, featuring images of statues, temples, and devotional art. On Pinterest, there are boards focused on Shivangna-themed home decor, clothing, and spiritual practices. Blogs and websites provide in-depth information about the significance of the name, rituals for honoring Shivangna, and the role of Shiva in Hindu mythology.
